learning.learning_goal: Compare two counted groups and connect “how many more,” difference, and subtraction.
learning.big_idea: Match one blue and one red. The extra blue buttons show the difference.
assumed_prior_knowledge: Count objects one by one up to 20 and know the last number said is the total.
Match one item from one group with one item from another group.

screens.label: Comparison 1
screens.title: How many more?
screens.body: First, count the blue and red buttons. Then see how many more blue buttons there are.
screens.callout: This is the first comparison lesson, not the first math lesson. You need to count objects to 20 and match them one to one. Earlier lessons are being built.

screens.label: Count
screens.title: How many blue buttons?

visual.ariaLabel: Ten blue buttons in the top row and five red buttons in the bottom row.

hints: Point to each blue button once. Count from left to right.
Count only the blue row. Stop when you reach its last button.

screens.label: Count
screens.title: How many red buttons?

visual.ariaLabel: Ten blue buttons in the top row and five red buttons in the bottom row.

hints: Point to each red button once. Count from left to right.
Count only the red row. Stop when you reach its last button.

visual.ariaLabel: Ten blue buttons above five red buttons. Rings form around five columns, each with one blue and one red button.
visual.message: Each ring joins one blue button and one red button.

screens.label: Discover
screens.title: How many blue buttons have no red match?

visual.ariaLabel: Five circled blue and red pairs, followed by five gold blue buttons without red buttons below them.
visual.message: The gold buttons have no red button below them. Count them.

choices.feedback: Yes. Five blue buttons have no red match. There are 5 more blue buttons than red buttons.

hints: Look for blue buttons outside the five circles.
Count only the gold buttons, one at a time.

screens.label: Language
screens.title: Two ways to ask the same question.

visual.ariaLabel: Five circled pairs and five extra gold blue buttons.
visual.message: The extra blue buttons are the difference.

screens.phraseMeaning: Find how far apart the two counts are.
screens.guidance: Here both questions ask for the extra blue buttons. That number is called the difference.

screens.label: Remember
screens.title: More? Difference? Find the extras.
screens.body: Subtract to find the difference: 10 − 5 = 5. Subtraction can compare two counts; it can also describe taking away.

screens.label: Misconception
screens.title: Does “more” always mean add?
screens.prompt: Ava has 14 stickers. Luis has 8. What is the difference in their sticker counts?

choices.feedback: Match 8 of Ava’s stickers with Luis’s 8. Six of Ava’s stickers remain unmatched, so the difference is 6.

hints: The question asks how far apart 14 and 8 are, not how many stickers they have together.
Start at 8 and count up to 14. How many steps did you count?

screens.label: Symbol
screens.title: Which subtraction finds the difference?

visual.ariaLabel: Five circled pairs and five extra blue buttons.
visual.message: Start with 10 blue. Match 5 red. How many blue are extra?

choices.feedback: Yes. Ten blue minus five matched blue leaves five extra blue buttons. The difference is 5.

hints: Start with the 10 blue buttons. Five have red matches.
Which sign lets you find how many of the 10 blue buttons have no match?

visual.ariaLabel: Five circled pairs and five extra blue buttons.

screens.label: Guided practice
screens.title: How many more blue blocks are there?

visual.message: Count the top row and the bottom row. Match one from each row, starting on the left.

choices.feedback: Yes. Seven blocks are matched across the rows. Four top blocks have no block below, so there are 4 more on top.

hints: Trace the first top block to the bottom block beneath it. Keep going until the bottom row ends.
Count the top blocks that have no block below them.

screens.label: Independent practice
screens.title: Solve without the model.
screens.prompt: Nia read 16 pages. Theo read 9 pages. How many more pages did Nia read?
hints: Imagine 16 marks for Nia and 9 for Theo. Match one from each group until Theo’s marks run out.
Count Nia’s unmatched marks. Or start at 9 and count up to 16.

screens.label: Recall
screens.title: Which exam wording asks for the same number?
screens.prompt: For 10 blue buttons and 5 red buttons, which question asks for the extra blue buttons?

choices.feedback: Yes. “Difference” asks how far apart the two counts are: 10 − 5 = 5.

hints: “In all” joins the two colors. We want the blue buttons with no red match.
Look for a question about how far apart the two counts are.

screens.label: Transfer
screens.title: Use the idea in a new setting.
screens.prompt: A blue notebook costs $18 and a red notebook costs $11. How much more does the blue notebook cost?

choices.feedback: $18 − $11 = $7, so the blue notebook costs $7 more.

hints: Compare the two prices. Is the question asking for their combined cost or how far apart they are?
Start at $11 and count up to $18. How much did the price increase?

screens.label: Reflect
screens.title: What did you discover?
screens.prompt: What does subtraction show when we compare two counts?

choices.text: It always means taking objects away.
It joins the counts into one total.
It finds the difference between the counts.

hints: We matched one blue with one red, then found the extra blue buttons.
Ten minus five tells how far apart ten and five are.

screens.title: You found the difference.
screens.body: “How many more?” and “What is the difference?” both ask for how far apart the counts are.
